message.content: {"ranking": [{"id": "patch_f8d57d590691", "failure_port": "o_wb_ack", "source_line": 582, "mechanism": "The public failure trace shows o_wb_ack asserting at cycle 6 (expected 0) then de-asserting at cycle 7 (expected 1), indicating the acknowledgment is being generated one cycle too early. The original source at line 582 unconditionally assigns o_wb_ack <= wb_stb on every clock edge. In the Wishbone bus protocol, wb_stb is only valid when i_wb_cyc is asserted. This patch adds the missing i_wb_cyc qualification so the ack only asserts during qualified bus cycles, aligning the acknowledgment timing with the bus protocol and the expected trace."}, {"id": "patch_350b815b2e75", "failure_port": "o_wb_ack", "source_line": 9820, "mechanism": "During FIFO write operations, the command state machine at line 9820 sets ll_fifo_wr <= 1'b1 based on r_use_fifo alone, without checking r_fifo_wr. This can cause spurious FIFO write initiation when r_use_fifo is set but r_fifo_wr is clear, leading to premature command completion and early o_wb_ack de-assertion observed at cycle 7. The patch adds the r_fifo_wr guard so FIFO write only starts when both FIFO usage and write direction are configured."}, {"id": "patch_0443cf09f504", "failure_port": "o_wb_ack", "source_line": 9820, "mechanism": "At line 9820 the condition r_use_fifo enables FIFO operations without verifying r_fifo_wr. When a read command incorrectly enables FIFO write path, the state machine advances prematurely, causing o_wb_ack to drop at cycle 7 instead of holding through the data phase. Adding the r_fifo_wr check ensures only actual write commands use the FIFO write path, stabilizing the ack waveform."}, {"id": "patch_e69de1c27f07", "failure_port": "o_wb_ack", "source_line": 9994, "mechanism": "The condition at line 9994 triggers FIFO operations on (r_use_fifo)&&(r_fifo_wr) without checking ll_fifo_rd_complete. If a previous FIFO read is still completing, this can cause overlapping FIFO transactions that corrupt the command state machine and produce the early o_wb_ack transitions seen at cycles 6-7. The patch adds the completion guard to serialize FIFO operations correctly."}, {"id": "patch_574faa6d7168", "failure_port": "o_wb_ack", "source_line": 9994, "mechanism": "Line 9994 enables FIFO write based on (r_use_fifo)&&(r_fifo_wr) without waiting for ll_fifo_rd_complete. When switching from read to write commands, a lingering read completion can overlap with the new write setup, disturbing the command state timing and causing the observed o_wb_ack mismatch at cycle 6 (actual 1 vs expected 0). Requiring ll_fifo_rd_complete ensures clean command boundaries."}, {"id": "patch_cef2e466558e", "failure_port": "o_wb_ack", "source_line": 9789, "mechanism": "At line 9789 the response token condition uses r_have_resp without qualifying r_use_fifo. For FIFO write commands, the state machine should only advance when both response is received and FIFO usage is configured. Without this guard, non-FIFO commands may incorrectly take the FIFO path or vice versa, desynchronizing the command state and producing the o_wb_ack timing errors at cycles 6-7."}, {"id": "patch_9ce4a09dbd52", "failure_port": "o_wb_ack", "source_line": 8636, "mechanism": "The pre_cmd_state signal at line 8636 enables command state machine advancement without checking ll_cmd_stb. If the low-level SPI transmitter is not idle (ll_cmd_stb=0), advancing the command state causes premature byte emission and early o_wb_ack assertion at cycle 6. Adding the ll_cmd_stb guard ensures command processing only proceeds when the SPI layer can accept new bytes."}, {"id": "patch_8cf8e76d1134", "failure_port": "o_wb_ack", "source_line": 9820, "mechanism": "Line 9820 uses r_use_fifo alone to enable FIFO operations in the command state machine. The patch adds r_have_resp qualification so FIFO write only starts after the SD card response token is received. Without this, FIFO write initiates immediately on command issue, running ahead of the card response and causing the state machine to complete early, which manifests as the o_wb_ack mismatch at cycle 7 (actual 0 vs expected 1)."}], "explanation": "The dominant failure is o_wb_ack asserting one cycle early (cycle 6 actual=1 expected=0) and de-asserting one cycle early (cycle 7 actual=0 expected=1). This pattern indicates the Wishbone acknowledgment is not properly qualified by the bus cycle (i_wb_cyc), and the command state machine is advancing prematurely due to missing guards on FIFO operations and response token handling. The top-ranked patch_f8d57d590691 directly fixes the ack generation by adding the i_wb_cyc qualification at the exact assignment site (line 582). The subsequent patches address upstream state machine timing issues: patches 350b815b2e75 and 0443cf09f504 guard FIFO write initiation with r_fifo_wr; patches e69de1c27f07 and 574faa6d7168 serialize FIFO read/write with ll_fifo_rd_complete; patch cef2e466558e qualifies FIFO path selection with r_use_fifo; patch 9ce4a09dbd52 gates command advancement on ll_cmd_stb; patch 8cf8e76d1134 delays FIFO write until r_have_resp. Together these stabilize the command/response/FIFO pipeline so o_wb_ack aligns with the bus-cycle-qualified protocol."}
